A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GRAPHFILTER study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendix A are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original fine-tuning experiments across three model backbones and six benchmarks, together with runtime measurements, ablations, and selected-data analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds experiments varying quality/diversity metrics and n-gram order.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes TF(v) from corpus-wide occurrence counts to within-sentence counts, revising the stated diversity weighting. Algorithm 1 also omits explicit deletion of already disconnected n-gram nodes. The greedy selection framework remains; these specification revisions do not establish that the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both use the same Magpie 300K training pool and evaluate MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag, GSM8K, AlpacaEval-2.0, and MT-Bench. Added ablations remain within this existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: The nine main baselines remain unchanged. However, Table 4 expands its component comparison to include RANDOM, ARMORM, and DEITA quality variants and MTLD-based alternatives, including SKYWORKRM; these configurations were absent from the corresponding v1 comparison.

E3.justification: New ablations introduce additional metric configurations and an n-gram-order sweep from 1 to 5, measuring graph-node counts alongside runtime and performance. Existing experiments retain their selection budgets, backbones, evaluation metrics, judges, and Appendix A training settings.

E4.justification: v2 extends the existing component ablations with alternative quality and diversity metrics and adds an n-gram-order performance/resource sensitivity study in Table 5. The original component-removal, n-gram-combination, instruction-versus-response, subset-characterization, and selection-budget analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added ablations retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark, runtime, and ablation values are retained, including v1 Table 5 as v2 Table 6. New Table 4 entries include overall scores of 46.61 for ARMORM plus TF-IDF and 47.47 for SUPERFILTER plus MTLD. New Table 5 reports n-gram-order scores, graph sizes, and runtimes.

T1.justification: The corpus-to-sentence revision of TF(v) in Section 3.3 changes a mathematical definition underlying the diversity score. The set-cover special-case argument, harmonic approximation-factor claim, and complexity discussion remain unchanged; no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims a set-cover formulation in the abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion. v1 presented that connection as a special case in Section 3.2. The central claims about balancing quality and diversity, benchmark performance, and efficiency otherwise remain.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the expanded metric experiments as evidence of flexibility and robustness, and the n-gram-order sweep as supporting trigrams for balancing performance and efficiency. Existing interpretations of instruction diversity, selected-data characteristics, and budget dependence are retained.

D1.justification: v2 removes the reproducibility statement promising code and scripts upon acceptance, along with several exact checkpoint links, including ARMORM and SKYWORKRM. Appendix A retains the baseline implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, and hardware. This reduces documented access information without establishing any actual resource withdrawal.

R1.justification: The PaLM 2 technical report citation, Anil et al. (2023b) in v1, is removed; the Gemini reference remains. Section 2 and the broader comparison with prior data-selection research are otherwise substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and portions of the introduction and conclusion are rewritten, Section 3.2 gains explanatory headings, and Section 5 loses its numbered subsections. Ethics and reproducibility sections give way to an impact statement and acknowledgements. Most technical prose and the main section sequence remain.

P2.justification: The manuscript is reformatted throughout from one column to two-column proceedings layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. The introductory overview figure is removed, Table 4 is expanded, a new Table 5 is added, and the retained budget chart receives revised sizing, ticks, and legend placement.

improvement.justification: The added metric substitutions and n-gram performance/runtime sweep strengthen the empirical justification for the design choices. These gains modestly outweigh the reduced code-release and checkpoint disclosures. The broader set-cover framing receives no additional formal support, so the revision offers a limited overall improvement.
